appraisal_events.evidence: "Le duc se parait de sa femme mais ne l'aimait pas. Très «suffisant», il détestait d'être interrompu... l'habitude d'être brutal avec elle... 'que diable! quand on s'appelle le marquis de Saint-Loup, on n'est pas dreyfusard'... M. de Guermantes prononça ces mots... avec emphase. Il savait pourtant bien que c'était une plus grande chose de s'appeler «le duc de Guermantes»."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly exposes M. de Guermantes as vain and domestically brutal, and shows his claimed absence of prejudice as rationalization, catching him in a further small vanity: he emphasizes the marquisate of Saint-Loup while privately knowing his own ducal title outranks it.

appraisal_events.evidence: "C'est surtout comique, répondit la duchesse, étant donné les idées de sa mère qui nous rase avec la Patrie française du matin au soir."
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchesse punctures her husband's rationalizing speech with an ironic aside mocking Mme de Marsantes as a tiresome nationalist zealot, made comic by her own son's opposite politics.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator strips away his self-presentation, exposing him directly as vain, hypocritical about prejudice, and habitually brutal with his wife.
She is mocked in absentia as a tiresome nationalist zealot, an irony sharpened by her son's opposing Dreyfusard politics.
She gets the ironic last word, using her wit to puncture her husband's rationalizing speech.
